concepts.def: Group 1: Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs
Group 7: F, Cl, Br, I, At
Group 0: He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe
More reactive halogen displaces less reactive

walkthroughs.body_html:
Reactivity increases down Group 1.

Outer electron is further from nucleus -> easier to lose.

All react with water: Li gently, K very vigorously.

Reactivity decreases down Group 7.

Outer shell further from nucleus -> harder to gain an electron.

Fluorine is yellow gas; chlorine green; bromine red-brown liquid; iodine purple solid.

Full outer shells -> very unreactive.

Boiling point increases down: He -269 C up to Xe -108 C.

Argon used in light bulbs; helium in balloons.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
